page: Microsoft Azure D4ds_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance provides 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The underlying hardware features a 48 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and cryptography acceleration via AES and SHA_NI.

This instance is provisioned with 154 GB of local SSD storage and is Premium Storage capable, allowing for high-performance external disk attachments. Virtualization is managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, ensuring dedicated CPU allocation. There are no bundled GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses included with this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates average single-core performance across stress-ng and Geekbench tests, alongside average single-threaded compression and decompression speeds. However, multi-core scaling and memory bandwidth are relatively weak, placing in the bottom quartile of tested systems. Database operations and Redis SET throughput also reflect lower-tier performance. Consequently, the D4ds_v5 is best suited for general-purpose workloads such as light web serving, basic application hosting, and development environments rather than memory-intensive or highly parallelized database tasks.
